core_obligations: Note that the colimit is a sheaf by construction, fix a member of the system, choose an affine etale covering of it, and observe that the covering is an etale covering by affine schemes after passing to reductions (proof lines 7912-7917).

Extend the covering along the system: using that all members have the same reduction, produce for each later member an affine formal algebraic space etale over it whose base change to the fixed member recovers the chosen piece, and verify compatibility of these pieces (proof lines 7917-7938).

Form the colimits of these pieces and show that the resulting morphism into the colimit of the members is etale, by the fact that a morphism from a quasi-compact scheme into a colimit factors through a member (proof lines 7934-7941).

Show that each colimit of pieces is an affine formal algebraic space: the transition maps are closed immersions as base changes of the given ones and induce isomorphisms on reductions, which is the hypothesis of the auxiliary statement on directed colimits of affine pieces (proof lines 7941-7951).
proof_roadmap: Choose a covering of one member and pass to reductions (proof lines 7912-7917).
Extend the covering along the directed system (proof lines 7917-7938).
The colimit morphism is etale, tested on quasi-compact schemes (proof lines 7934-7941).
Each piece is affine by the auxiliary colimit statement (proof lines 7941-7951).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a directed system of formal algebraic spaces whose transition maps are closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on the reductions, the colimit, taken in fppf sheaves, is again a formal algebraic space (statement lines 7902-7910). The proof constructs the presentation explicitly. A member of the system is fixed and one of its affine etale coverings is chosen, so that the covering is an etale covering by affine schemes after passing to reductions (proof lines 7912-7917). The covering is then extended to the whole system: since the reductions of all members agree, the etale covering of the reduction of the fixed member corresponds to an affine formal algebraic space etale over every other member, and the identification lemma for the affine etale site shows both that base changing it back gives the original piece and that the pieces are compatible along the system (proof lines 7917-7938). Taking the colimits of the pieces over the system produces a morphism into the colimit of the members, which is etale because any morphism into the colimit from a quasi-compact scheme factors through a member, so it remains to see that each collected piece is an affine formal algebraic space; this follows because the transition maps between the pieces are closed immersions, as base changes of the given ones, and induce isomorphisms on reductions, which is the situation of the auxiliary statement on colimits of affine pieces (proof lines 7938-7951). The claim is H2: the argument is a construction carried along a directed system, and its three ingredients -- extending the covering along the system, showing the resulting morphism is etale by testing on quasi-compact schemes, and reducing each piece to the affine case -- are each stated with their reason.
